newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rebate plan raises October car sales.
newsitem.headline: French rebate plan raises October car sales.

text.p: New car sales in France surged in October as a government rebate offer once again breathed life into the French car market.
The rise was also boosted because of weak car sales in October 1995, which were hit by the sluggish start of a different government sale-boosting scheme.

French carmakers association CCFA said new car sales in France were up 24.7 percent to 202,482 in October, surprising most analysts. Analysts continue to expect car sales to drop in the coming months due to the end of the rebate scheme.
Sales by France's two carmakers, PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault also rose, but their market share fell.
For the first ten months of the year, car sales in France were 14.7 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
CCFA said the rise was boosted by a last-minute rush to buy cars before the end of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's old-car-for-new rebate plan.
The plan expired on September 30 but CCFA said some of October's rise was due to sales billed at the end of September but registered in the first few days of October.
CCFA said another factor boosting the month's results was the comparative weakness of October 1995 car sales. In October 1995 car sales fell 6.3 percent compared to a year earlier.
Sales were lower then because another car rebate plan, launched from the beginning of October 1995, did not boost sales until the second half of the month, CCFA said.
PSA sales were up 5.9 percent to 55,717 cars, after a 13.1 percent rise in Peugeot car sales and a 4.9 percent drop in Citroen car sales.
Renault sales were up 28.7 percent to 56,363.

The market share controlled by the two French car makers dropped both year over year and cumulatively for 1996. On a year-over-year basis, French market share was 55.4 percent in October compared to 59.5 percent a year ago.
In the first ten months of 1996, French carmakers' market share in France was 56.2 percent, down from 60.4 percent in the January to October period of 1995.

Foreign car sales rose 37.2 percent to 90,380 compared to a year ago and represented 44.6 percent of the market. Japanese carmakers controlled 4.3 percent of the market as their sales rose 38.9 percent to 8,742.
The biggest gainer for the month was Fiat, which increased its sales by 74.1 percent compared to a year ago, bringing sales to 18,969. Its market share was 9.4 percent.
